questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
Identify the correct decreasing order of acid strength for the following compounds:

$\text{(I)}\text{HClO,}\text{(II)}\text{HBrO,}\text{(III)}\text{HIO}$
questions.solution:
The acidic character of hypohalous acid depends on the electronegativity of halogen. As the electronegativity value of halogen increases the acidic strength of hypohalous acid increases.

Here, Electronegativity of atom $\text{X}$ ($\text{Cl,}\text{Br}$ or $\text{I}$) attached to $\text{O}$ decreases down the group, polarity of OH bond decreases, acid strength decreases. It means more the electronegativity of the halogen atom, more the tendency to pull electron and weaker the $\text{O} - \text{H}$ bond and hence proton ${\text{(H}}^{\text{+}} \text{)}$ can easily be removed.

Consider Electronic configuration of $M^{+}$
${}_{\text{23}} V^{+} {⇒}_{\text{18}} \text{[Ar]}{\text{4s}^{1} {\text{3d}^{3}$

Removal of second electron from stable configuration of ${}_{\text{18}} \text{[Ar]}{\text{4s}^{0} {\text{3d}^{5}$ will require very high energy input i.e. $\text{(Cr)}$ as it will disturb the stable electronic configuration of ${\text{3d}^{5}$ (half filled subshell).

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
The atomic number of elements $\text{A, B, C}$ and $\text{D}$ are $\text{Z} - \text{1,}\text{Z,}\text{Z}\text{+}\text{1,}\text{Z}\text{+}\text{2}$ respectively. If $\text{B}$ is a noble gas, choose the correct option
(i) $\text{(A)}$ has higher electron affinity
(ii) $\left(\text{C}\right)$ exists in + 2 oxidation state
(iii) $\left(\text{D}\right)$ is an alkaline earth metal
questions.solution:
Atomic number of $\left(B\right) = Z$ and is a noble gas

Atomic number of $\left(A\right) = Z - 1$ (i.e., is a Halogen)

Atomic number $\left(C\right), = Z + 1$ (i.e., is a alkali metal)

At number of $\left(D\right) = Z + 2$ (i.e., alkaline earth metal)

Hence, element $\left(A\right)$ must be a Halogen, so has highest electron affinity among the given species. $\left(C\right) .$ is an alkali metal and $\left(D\right)$ is an alkaline earth metal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: In graph of atomic volume versus atomic weight, the elements corresponding to peaks in the curve belong to
questions.solution:
If we see the atomic mass versus atomic volume curve, we will notice the following features:

  • Alkali metals such as $\text{Na,}\text{K,}\text{Rb}$ which have similar properties occur as peaks of the curve.
  • Halogen elements like $\text{F,}\text{Cl,}\text{Br,}$ which have similar properties occur at the rising or the ascending part of the curve.
  • Noble gases such as $\text{Ne,}\text{Ar,}\text{Kr}$ which have similar properties occur just before the alkali elements.
  • Hydrogen and Helium seem to be exception to the rule.

questions.q: The effective nuclear charge of an element with three valence electrons is 2.60. What is the minimum atomic number of the element?
questions.solution:
As effective nuclear charge is 2.60 and valence shell contain 3 electrons so the minimum number of main shells for the given element are two i.e., (n = 2) and its configuration will be $1s^{2}, 2s^{2}, 2p^{1}$.

Hence the given element has 5 electrons in all.

Also, for a neutral atom.

As number of electrons = atomic number = 5.

Thus, the atomic number of the element is 5.

In general the ionic radius increases on moving from top to bottom in group and decreases on moving from left to right in period. So, Na^{+}& > Li^{+}& and Mg^{2+}& > Be^{2+}.&

The size of Mg^{2+}& is however smaller than Li^{+}. Despite the Mg atom having a slightly larger atomic size, the Mg^{2+} ion is marginally smaller in size than the Li^{+} ion because of its higher nuclear charge

$\text{N}{\text{a}_{0.98\text{Å}^{+} > \text{L}{\text{i}_{0.68\text{Å}^{+} > \text{M}{\text{g}_{0.65\text{Å}^{2 +} > \text{B}{\text{e}_{0.62\text{Å}^{2 +}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
Which of the following statements is (are) incorrect?

(i) Percentage ionic character in $CsCl$ bond is $ 55%$. (Electronegativity values of $Cs$ and $Cl$ are $0.7$ and $3.0$ respectively)

(ii) From ${H}_{2}O$ to ${H}_{3}O^{+}$ , the geometry around $O$ atom changes drastically.

(iii) The most stable oxidation state for element with atomic number $113$ is expected to be $+ 2.$

(iv) The ${2}^{nd}$ ionization energy of $Ca$ is greater than ${1}^{st}$ ionization energy of it but lower than ${2}^{nd}$ ionization energy of K.
questions.solution:
$( a )$ Ionic character

$% ioniccharacter = 16 ( {x}_{A} - {x}_{B} ) + 3.5{( {x}_{A} - {x}_{B} )}^{2}$

where, ${x}_{A} - {x}_{B} =$Difference in electro-negativity of bonded atoms.$16 \times ( 3.0 - 0.7 ) + 3.5 \times {( 3.0 - 0.7 )}^{2} = 55.32 %$

$( b )$ Geometry for both the species is tetrahedral, as in both 'O' is $sp^{3}$ hybridised

$\left(c\right)113 = \left[Rn\right]5f^{14}6d^{10}7s^{2}7p^{1} =$ Due to inert pair effect $7s^{2}$electron do not take part in bond formation, so, most stable oxidation state is $+ 1 .

$( d )$ Successive ionization energies are higher for every element. ${2}^{nd}$ ionization of K happens from $3s^{2}3p^{6}$ configuration which is an inert gas configuration and for $Ca$ it happens from $4s^{1}$. So, K has higher second ionisation energy than Ca.$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
How many of these elements have more first ionization energy then boron
$Li, Be, C, N, O, F, Ne$ .
questions.solution:
Here the order of first ionization energy is as follows
$Ne > F > N > O > C > Be > B > Li$
Hence six elements have more first ionization energy then boron.

The correct code for stability, of oxidation states for given cations is
I. $Pb^{2 +} > Pb^{4 +}, Tl^{+} < Tl^{3 +}$ II. $Bi^{3 +} < Sb^{3 +}, Sn^{2 +} < Sn^{4 +}$
III. $Pb^{2 +} > Pb^{4 +}, Bi^{3 +} > Bi^{5 +}$ IV. $Tl^{3 +} < In^{3 +}, Sn^{2 +} > Sn^{4 +}$
V. $Sn^{2 +} < Pb^{2 +}, Sn^{4 +} > Pb^{4 +}$ VI. $Sn^{2 +} < Pb^{2 +}, Sn^{4 +} < Pb^{4 +}$
questions.solution:
Due to inert effect the stability of lower oxidation state gradually increases while stability of higher oxidation state gradually decreases down the group in elements of group 13th to 15th. So correct order are
III. $Pb^{2 +} > Pb^{4 +}, Bi^{3 +} > Bi^{5 +}$
IV. $Sn^{2 +} < Pb^{2 +}, Sn^{4 +} < Pb^{4 +}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.solution:
As you go from left to right in the periodic table, the acidic strength goes on increasing. Also, as you increases the oxidation state of the central atom, the acidic strength increases.

The more the electronegativity and oxidation number of the central atom (Cl), more is the acidic character.
